Two recorded calls to the 86ff contract
Research date: 29 September 2026. Scope: a bounded, read-only review of two existing transactions
involving 0xe6df4ca976f3fec8da89efec332dc2245f0a86ff. This addresses what these transactions demonstrate
about token withdrawals; it is not a complete audit of the contract or its access controls.
Finding
Neither selected transaction demonstrates an asset withdrawal. The FdbEE transaction successfully
reads a cETH allowance. The b157 transaction has a successful outer receipt but a reverted internal
delegated call. Treating either outer success status as proof that tokens were withdrawn would
misdescribe the execution evidence.
These results do not prove that 86ff never enabled withdrawals in other transactions. They establish the
behavior of these two selected records. The contract has no verified source in the preceding discovery
batch, so this note does not infer public access, ownership or arbitrary-token withdrawal rights from a
function selector or the presence of multiple callers.
FdbEE transaction: allowance observation, no token transfer
Transaction 0x57ef…dacd occurred at block 26,687,406, 2 June 2026, 19:17:45 UTC, hash 
0x4349dbf0c25a6741c9dee03c84b05c5002f12dece39d373e54d7572fc33bdd99. The sender was 
0xfdbee32bcf68bb0ced033200373384a619c71967; the destination was 86ff. Its receipt reports success and contains
no logs.
The historical trace contains only two frames: the outer call to 86ff and an inner static call to 
0x4ddc2d193948926d02f9b1fe9e1daa0718270ed5. The latter contract reports symbol cETH at this block. The inner
call reads the allowance from 86ff to FdbEE and returns the maximum unsigned 256-bit value.
This supports a specific positive observation: the token contract reported that allowance for those two
addresses during the transaction. It does not show when or how the allowance was established. No 
approve, transfer, transferFrom, token redemption or native-currency payment appears in this execution
trace. There is no observed withdrawal amount to report.
A token allowance is also not a record that FdbEE owns 86ff, owns cETH's underlying lending protocol, or
controls every asset held by 86ff. Each is a separate claim. This review does not convert the observed
allowance into a claim about the authorization rules of every 86ff operation.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 31

b157 transaction: successful wrapper, reverted internal call
Transaction 0x2b6f…8de5 occurred at block 25,967,897, 8 March 2026, 01:41:15 UTC, hash 
0x8bd832c4fe1d3d1ce7d9c762714be1414f1bb87478e3964acfe14b1f4afb609a. The sender was 
0xb1573ff4421bf7f0b5d18aa9723f01a79930c68e; the destination was 86ff. Its receipt reports success and contains
one log emitted by 86ff.
The trace again contains two frames. The second is a delegatecall from 86ff to itself, which reports 
Reverted and has no subcalls. The outer frame nevertheless completes successfully. Consequently, the
receipt's overall success must not be applied to the failed internal operation.
The recorded input contains the copied WETH address, but the actual trace does not reach that token
contract. An address appearing in input bytes is not an executed token call. There is no observed WETH
transfer, deposit, withdrawal, native-currency payment or Aave interaction in this transaction. The 86ff
log has not been assigned a source-verified event name; it is not treated as an ERC-20 Transfer event or
proof of an asset movement.
Evidence and limits
The observations use eth_getTransactionReceipt, trace_transaction, eth_getBlockByNumber and a token-symbol
getter through https://rpc.pulsechain.com. Block numbers and hashes are specified individually above.
These are one-provider observations, not an independently verified state proof. No transaction,
simulation, impersonation, constructed withdrawal call or state change was performed.
Raw evidence is preserved under ignored artifacts/parb-wallet-debt-positions-20260929/86ff_observations/:
each sender's receipt, historical trace and block metadata, plus the cETH symbol read. The selected
hashes came from the preceding recent-transaction discovery record; that limited discovery list is not an
exhaustive contract history.
Any stronger claim that anyone can withdraw any token would require evidence of the actual
authorization logic and the relevant successful asset movements. These two records establish an
allowance read and a caught internal failure, not that universal withdrawal claim. They likewise do not
establish debt-token ownership, repayment, profit allocation or the owner of 86ff.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 32
